Starting the accumulator at one
Taking only the first element

questions.explanation: reduce folds every element into the accumulator starting from zero, producing the sum 1824. The initial value is the seed, not an extra element. Run line by line, the closing console.log emits 1824.
questions.hint: The accumulator starts at the supplied initial value.

questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving arrays — foreach.

options.misconception: Confusing count with accumulated total
Only the first callback runs in their view

questions.explanation: forEach calls the callback once per element, adding each to sum, which reaches 1806. forEach returns undefined but the closure updates the outer variable. Both the direct number 1806 and the equivalent sum 903 plus 903 match, whereas 1797 and 3 come from only the first callback runs in their view and confusing count with accumulated total.
questions.hint: The callback runs once for every array element.

questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving strings — charat.

options.misconception: Reading index zero instead of one
Guessing an unrelated character from the string
Reading the final digit

questions.explanation: charAt returns the character at the given zero-based index; index 1 of '1798' is '7'. Index zero would be the first digit, not the second. Walking the snippet in order, the output is 7.
questions.hint: String positions start counting at zero.

questions.subject: JAVASCRIPT
questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving strings — slice.

options.misconception: Stopping after one character
Keeping the removed first character
Assuming slice copies the whole string

questions.explanation: With one argument, slice returns everything from that index to the end, dropping the first character of '1799'. The result is '799'. Working through the snippet, the printed result is 799.
questions.hint: A single slice index means from there to the end.
